published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'We study a free, linear, massless scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling in the context of perturbation theory about the flat spacetime/vacuum solution, and we modify the perturbed semiclassical equations by the "reduction of order" procedure to eliminate spurious solutions. We also restrict attention to the limit in which the lengthscales determined by the state and metric are much larger than the Planck length. At first order in the metric and state perturbations, and for pure states of the scalar field, we find that the ANEC integral vanishes ... For mixed states, the ANEC integral can be negative. However, we prove that if we average the ANEC integral transverse to the geodesic, using a suitable Planck scale smearing function, a strictly positive result is obtained in all cases except for the trivial flat spacetime/vacuum solution. Similar results hold for pure states at second order in perturbation theory, when we additionally specialize to the situation where incoming classical gravitational radiation does not dominate the first order metric perturbation. These results suggest ... that if traversable wormholes do exist as self-consistent solutions of the semiclassical equations, they cannot be macroscopic but must be "Planck scale".' Sec. I C (p.5): 'We wish to consider a one-parameter family (with parameter denoted by eps) of spacetimes (M, g_ab(eps)) and quantum states satisfying Eq. (1.1) [G_ab = 8 pi <T_ab>], with the spacetime reducing to Minkowski spacetime and the quantum state reducing to the vacuum state when eps = 0'; eq. (1.6) omega_in(eps) = omega_in,0 + eps omega^(1)_in + eps^2 omega^(2)_in + O(eps^3); eq. (1.7) g_ab(eps) = eta_ab + eps h^(1)_ab + eps^2 h^(2)_ab + O(eps^3). Sec. V (p.27): 'we would like to show that the ANEC integral along any complete, achronal, null geodesic in the spacetime (M, eta_ab + eps h^(1)_ab + eps^2 h^(2)_ab) is non-negative to order eps^2. However, this desired positivity property actually fails ... Nevertheless, we do obtain a positivity result involving a transversely smeared version of the ANEC integral.' FW's OWN statement of semiclassical gravity's domain (p.2, second of three possibilities): objects that 'always lie outside the domain of validity of the semiclassical theory, either because the curvature scales are Planckian somewhere in the corresponding spacetimes, or because the quantum fluctuations in the stress tensor are comparable to its expected value.' On why perturbation theory (p.4): 'In order to analyze generic solutions to Eq. (1.1), we will be forced to resort to perturbation theory about the trivial solution, namely, Minkowski spacetime with the quantum field in the vacuum state.' On general spacetimes (p.5): 'Our perturbative result suggests that something similar may be true in general spacetimes, and consequently that the behavior of solutions in semiclassical gravity -- within the domain of validity of that theory -- may be qualitatively similar to classical solutions.'
published_hypotheses: H1 matter: a single free, linear (non-self-interacting), massless scalar field with arbitrary curvature coupling xi (abstract; p.3 'Our analysis applies only to non-self-interacting quantum fields'; p.5)
H2 self-consistency: spacetime and state obey the semiclassical Einstein equation G_ab = 8 pi <T_ab> (eq. 1.1), whose only source is the quantum field's <T_ab> -- no classical matter

H3 one-parameter family: (g_ab(eps), omega(eps)) reducing to Minkowski + vacuum at eps = 0 (p.5); results hold through O(eps^2), terms O(eps^3) dropped (eqs 1.6-1.7); no remainder estimate on the pages read
H4 reduction of order applied to the perturbed semiclassical equations to remove runaway/spurious solutions (abstract; Sec. IV, p.27 eqs 4.20, 4.23)
H5 long wavelengths: lengthscales of state and metric >> Planck length (abstract; alpha >> 1; eq. 4.23 carries unknown corrections O((ln alpha)^2/alpha^6))
H6 states: Hadamard 2-point distributions with positivity; states characterised by in-data at past null infinity J^- under 'suitable asymptotic conditions' (p.5)

H7 second-order pure-state result additionally needs incoming classical gravitational radiation not to dominate h^(1) (abstract; p.4); the explicit <T^(2)_ab[h1,h1], omega_in,0> is not evaluated and an approximate form (3.59) is used (p.27)

H8 the geodesic is complete and achronal (eq. 1.5; p.27); the conclusion is TRANSVERSELY SMEARED ANEC with a Planck-scale smearing function -- unsmeared ANEC fails (mixed states at first order; pure states at second order)
H9 globally hyperbolic spacetime (Sec. I B, p.3)
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION DRIFT (the substantive one) -- throatmass.py:68-72 ('If Flanagan-Wald, Anderson-Molina-Paris-Mottola and Kontou are right that eps ~ 1 lies outside semiclassical gravity's domain, the corridor is not refuted -- it is placed beyond the theory's jurisdiction'), carried into ledger.py:1683-1686 and LEDGER.md:204 ('the corridor is EXPELLED rather than refuted'). On the pages read FW make eps small a hypothesis of their ANALYSIS ('we will be forced to resort to perturbation theory', p.4), not a boundary of the THEORY: their stated domain criterion (p.2) is Planckian curvature somewhere or stress fluctuations comparable to the mean, and p.5 speaks of general spacetimes 'within the domain of validity of that theory'. eps ~ O(1) places the corridor outside FW's THEOREM, not (per FW) outside semiclassical gravity. Restatements agree: Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 ('After a detailed discussion of the range of validity of the semiclassical Einstein equation, they considered second order perturbations'); Graham-Olum 0705.3193 p.3 ('Condition 1 should be expected to hold only in cases where the curvature is well below the Planck scale'). Scope: pages 6-26 and 28-49 unread -- 'not found on the pages read', not 'FW never say'. The sentence is conditional ('If ... are right'), so it asserts nothing false; its antecedent, as attributed to FW, is not FW's claim on the pages read. Recorded, not repaired.

WORDING (a discrepancy, not an error) -- canonical/tree name FW's content a 'validity condition' with parameter 'eps'. In FW eps is a formal family parameter (rescalable); only eps*h^(1) has a size. The tree's identification eps ~ h ~ 0.5 is the natural reading and is kept; FW state no numerical threshold for eps.

KIND -- canonical 'theorem'. FW write 'we prove' (abstract) for the smeared-ANEC positivity, but within perturbation theory, after reduction of order, and at second order using an approximate equation with unknown corrections O(ln alpha/alpha^6) (p.27). A theorem inside an approximation scheme; the tree does not lean on it as more.

later_literature.ref: N. Graham & K. D. Olum, 'Achronal averaged null energy condition', arXiv:0705.3193, PRD 76 064001 (2007)
later_literature.what: p.4: FW 'found violations of ANEC in self-consistent perturbation theory about Minkowski space. Although they stated ANEC in the achronal form, they did not discuss ... whether the ANEC violations that they found were on chronal or achronal geodesics ... at second order ANEC could be violated. In this case, the geodesics in question are chronal.' Proposes self-consistent ACHRONAL ANEC; p.3 restricts it to 'curvature well below the Planck scale' -- a domain criterion in curvature, not in metric amplitude.

later_literature.ref: E.-A. Kontou & K. Sanders, 'Energy conditions in general relativity and quantum field theory', arXiv:2003.01815, CQG 37 193001 (2020)
later_literature.what: 'Perhaps the best support to date for the general validity of the AANEC ... comes from Flanagan and Wald' -- restates FW's hypotheses exactly as read here (perturbations about Minkowski/vacuum, second order, no dominant incoming radiation, long-wavelength limit, transverse averaging over several Planck areas); 'Kontou and Olum [83, 124] used a similar argument to prove AANEC in spacetimes with small curvature'; AANEC 'has no known physically reasonable counter-examples'.

later_literature.ref: E.-A. Kontou & K. D. Olum, AANEC in curved spacetime with small curvature (Kontou-Sanders refs [83], [124])
later_literature.what: a proof of achronal ANEC for the minimally coupled scalar beyond FW's flat-background perturbation, still under a small-curvature hypothesis; does not reach eps*h ~ O(1).

later_literature.ref: D. Urban & K. D. Olum, 'Averaged null energy condition violation in a conformally flat spacetime', arXiv:0910.5925, PRD 81 024039 (2010)
later_literature.what: abstract: achronal ANEC violated, arbitrarily, by a conformally coupled scalar in a conformally flat 3+1 spacetime. Kontou-Sanders: 'all these violations are only known for test fields, so the semiclassical Einstein equation is not imposed' -- so it does not contradict FW, whose hypothesis H2 is exactly self-consistency.

lacked_data: FW's conclusion rests on no measured datum: its inputs are the free scalar field, the semiclassical equation, and the Planck length as a unit (their result is scale-free in Planck units). What FW lacked in 1996 was MATHEMATICS, stated by FW themselves on the pages read: the explicit <T^(2)_ab[h1,h1], omega_in,0> (p.27, 'has not been evaluated'), a reduction-of-order scheme for the full nonlocal equation (p.27, 'it is not obvious if and/or how the reduction of order procedure could be applied to the full, nonlinear semiclassical Einstein equation'), and interacting fields (p.3). What came later (Graham-Olum 2007, Urban-Olum 2010, Kontou-Olum's small-curvature AANEC proof, Kontou-Sanders 2020) is also mathematical; none supplies a non-perturbative result at eps*h ~ O(1), and none contradicts FW inside their hypotheses (Urban-Olum's violations are test-field, outside H2; Graham-Olum narrow the ANEC violations FW found to chronal geodesics). No datum has moved (h = 0.5 re-derived; l_P unchanged). Evidence therefore runs AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result: FW is not inaccurate for lack of data -- it is incomplete by its own declared scope (perturbative, free field), and that incompleteness is exactly why throatmass.py declines it. The one place later reading bears on the tree: FW's own domain criterion (Planckian curvature / fluctuations ~ mean) is NOT met by the corridor's curvature at any a >> l_P (rederive C3), so FW supply no support for the 'expulsion' reading at throatmass.py:68-72; the fluctuation criterion is not evaluated here and remains open.
grade_evidence: Two uses. (i) throatmass.py:62-64, :161 -- 'Flanagan-Wald is NOT applied: h ~ 0.5 ... makes eps ~ O(1) and their one-parameter perturbative family hypothesis fails.' STANDS: FW's results are through O(eps^2) about Minkowski+vacuum (p.5 eqs 1.6-1.7; p.27), h = 0.5 re-derived exactly (rederive A1), successive-order ratio 0.5 with an unbounded truncation remainder of 0.5-12.5 % (B1); the corridor also fails H2/H3 on class membership, since its h is sourced by a classical M not in FW's family. (ii) throatmass.py:68-72 / ledger.py:1683-1686 / LEDGER.md:204 -- the 'expulsion' conditional attributes to FW the claim that eps ~ 1 lies outside SEMICLASSICAL GRAVITY'S DOMAIN. On the pages read FW state that domain in terms of Planckian curvature or fluctuations ~ mean (p.2) and treat perturbation theory as a limitation of their analysis (p.4, p.5); two restatements agree (2003.01815; 0705.3193 p.3). The result, as FW state it, places eps ~ O(1) outside their THEOREM only -- a smaller claim than the tree's conditional reads into it. Hence NARROWED, not STANDS. Not WRONG: nothing in FW is refuted; the footnote [90] closed form and its expansion check exactly (D1, D2); no misprint found. Not OPEN: the statement and hypotheses were read at source (pages 1-5, 27, 50). The narrowing is bounded by the unread pages 6-26, 28-49.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: a passage on FW's unread pages (6-26, 28-49; esp. Sec. II-III on the 'nature of the semiclassical Einstein equation' and Appendix E) in which FW themselves place O(1) metric deviations, or strong fields generally, outside semiclassical gravity's domain -- then the attribution at throatmass.py:68-72 is FW's own. To WRONG for the tree's decline (not for FW): a demonstration that the corridor IS a member of FW's family (flat+vacuum at eps = 0, sourced by the quantum field alone) with eps*h << 1 -- excluded by h = 0.5 as computed. To DATA-DEPENDENT: none foreseeable; the conclusion depends on no measured datum. Evaluating FW's second domain criterion (stress-tensor fluctuations ~ mean) at the corridor could move the 'expulsion' question independently of FW's perturbative scope.
